plan_a_advantages: More frequent easy runs build a stronger aerobic base.
The longer long run (80 minutes) more closely mimics race distances and intensities.

reasoning: Plan A is the better training plan for a trail runner aiming to become faster. It incorporates more frequent, shorter runs, which is crucial for building consistent speed and improving running economy – key factors for trail running performance. While Plan B includes cross-training, it lacks the focused volume of easy runs that are essential for developing the aerobic base needed for faster times. Plan A’s longer, controlled long run (80 minutes) also better simulates the demands of a trail race, whereas Plan B’s is shorter and at a lower intensity.
